From ce3015b7212e96db426d0c36f80fd159c91155d1 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Tsuchiya Yuto <kitakar@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2021 01:19:41 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] media: atomisp: add missing media_device_cleanup() in
 atomisp_unregister_entities()

After the commit 9832e155f1ed ("[media] media-device: split media
initialization and registration"), calling media_device_cleanup()
is needed it seems. However, currently it is missing for the module
unload path.

Note that for the probe failure path, it is already added in
atomisp_register_entities().

This patch adds the missing call of media_device_cleanup() in
atomisp_unregister_entities().

Fixes: a49d25364dfb ("staging/atomisp: Add support for the Intel IPU v2")
Signed-off-by: Tsuchiya Yuto <kitakar@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab+huawei@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/staging/media/atomisp/pci/atomisp_v4l2.c b/drivers/staging/media/atomisp/pci/atomisp_v4l2.c
index 1e324f1f656e..0511c454e769 100644
--- a/drivers/staging/media/atomisp/pci/atomisp_v4l2.c
+++ b/drivers/staging/media/atomisp/pci/atomisp_v4l2.c
@@ -1182,6 +1182,7 @@ static void atomisp_unregister_entities(struct atomisp_device *isp)
 
 	v4l2_device_unregister(&isp->v4l2_dev);
 	media_device_unregister(&isp->media_dev);
+	media_device_cleanup(&isp->media_dev);
 }
 
 static int atomisp_register_entities(struct atomisp_device *isp)
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/staging/media/atomisp/pci/atomisp_v4l2.c`**
   - A new line was added to the `atomisp_unregister_entities` function:
     - `media_device_cleanup(&isp->media_dev);`
   - This line is responsible for cleaning up the media device when the entities are unregistered, addressing a missing cleanup call in the module unload path.

### Relationships
- The modification in `atomisp_v4l2.c` is directly related to the need for proper resource management during the unregistration of media entities. The patch addresses a previously identified issue where `media_device_cleanup()` was not called during the module unload process, which could lead to resource leaks or undefined behavior. This change complements the existing cleanup logic already present in the `atomisp_register_entities` function for probe failure scenarios. The patch is a corrective measure to ensure that the media device is properly cleaned up when the module is unloaded, thereby enhancing the stability and reliability of the driver.

Here is the commit message:
media: atomisp: add missing media_device_cleanup() in
 atomisp_unregister_entities()

After the commit 9832e155f1ed ("[media] media-device: split media
initialization and registration"), calling media_device_cleanup()
is needed it seems. However, currently it is missing for the module
unload path.

Note that for the probe failure path, it is already added in
atomisp_register_entities().

This patch adds the missing call of media_device_cleanup() in
atomisp_unregister_entities().

Fixes: a49d25364dfb ("staging/atomisp: Add support for the Intel IPU v2")
Signed-off-by: Tsuchiya Yuto <kitakar@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab+huawei@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the absence of a call to `media_device_cleanup()` in the `atomisp_unregister_entities()` function, which is necessary for properly cleaning up resources associated with the media device during the module unload process. This oversight can lead to resource leaks or undefined behavior when the module is unloaded, as the cleanup process was only implemented for probe failure scenarios in `atomisp_register_entities()`.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void atomisp_unregister_entities(struct atomisp_device *isp)
 {
 	unsigned int i;
 	struct v4l2_subdev *sd, *next;
 
 	for (i = 0; i < isp->num_of_streams; i++)
 		atomisp_subdev_unregister_entities(&isp->asd[i]);
 	atomisp_tpg_unregister_entities(&isp->tpg);
 	atomisp_file_input_unregister_entities(&isp->file_dev);
 	for (i = 0; i < ATOMISP_CAMERA_NR_PORTS; i++)
 		atomisp_mipi_csi2_unregister_entities(&isp->csi2_port[i]);
 
 	list_for_each_entry_safe(sd, next, &isp->v4l2_dev.subdevs, list)
 		v4l2_device_unregister_subdev(sd);
 
 	v4l2_device_unregister(&isp->v4l2_dev);
 	media_device_unregister(&isp->media_dev);
+	media_device_cleanup(&isp->media_dev);
 }
